notes: NIDCD says 'human'; the outline says 'mammalian'. Corwin & Cotanche's abstract notes loss of cochlear hair cells 'has been presumed to result in a permanent hearing deficit because the production of these cells normally ceases before birth' (mammals). Mammalian regeneration is an active research area (Wu 2020 mentions 'clinical trials of therapeutics designed to regrow hair cells are underway'), so say 'in us, they don't grow back on their own'. Do not imply a cure is close or available.

notes: Sha 2001's base-vs-apex survival data are drug/culture experiments in guinea pigs, not noise in people; use it only for 'the base is intrinsically more fragile'. Wu 2020/2021 (human autopsy) support 'most loss at high frequencies' and link it partly to noise. 'Why' is not fully settled; offer the reasons as 'one reason' (Sha: lower antioxidant levels in basal OHCs). Also note: noise damage often centres on a specific region (the classic audiogram 'notch'; Samara: 'the characteristic notch in the audiogram'), but no opened source gave the notch frequency; don't say '4 kHz notch' unless the fact checker sources it.

claim: Without outer hair cells, the amplifier is gone: in animal studies destroying them raised hearing thresholds by some 50 dB and blurred or removed the ear's sharp frequency tuning, so quiet sounds vanish and sounds blur together.
